comment: (2026-10-03T00:15:00Z). Read by tests/test_epg_match.py; no number here
This is the PRECISION half of M4-01's acceptance criterion, which
docs/PLAN-M4.md states and the M4 round never ran. The audit is
`oracle` is the point of the fixture. Each entry's plutoId is the
channel id Pluto itself uses: the installed playlist carries it inside
that row's stream URL and the guide carries it as the channel id. The
matcher reads neither -- it joins on the name -- so when the programme
that lands on a row is the programme of the channel whose id that row's
URL names, two independent identifiers agree and the pair is right for a
reason the code under test did not supply (CLAUDE.md rule 14). nowTitle
is unique per entry so the title alone says which guide channel won.
channelTotal 11 = 5 oracle pairs + 1 cross-channel pair + 2 country-
qualifier rows + 2 News12 rows dropped as ambiguous + 1 Tennis row.
matched 6 = the 5 oracle pairs plus the cross-channel pair, which is
the defect: D-EPG-5 is in the matched count, not outside it.
warnings: 4 programmes for channels not in the playlist dropped

why: The matcher's key folds + to a space, so Bloomberg Television and
Bloomberg TV+ become one name. normalize_id_text, the project's own
fold, keeps + 'because they are the difference between two channels
rather than noise inside one' -- so the project already holds the rule
that says this pair is two channels, and the matcher does not use it.
This entry asserts TODAY's behaviour. When D-EPG-5 is repaired the
pair disappears, status.matched becomes 5 and this block moves to
`unmatched`. The test that reads it says so in its docstring.

the + fold makes it collide with News12LongIsland, so both are dropped
